# Sampling versioned artwork catalogues

Tate remains the only method-development publisher. Reserve three independently published object tables from Cleveland Museum of Art, The Museum of Modern Art, and the National Gallery of Art. Each institution distributes its own collection in a versioned tabular repository. They were chosen for public version history, record identity, metadata reuse terms, and availability across the calendar period. Source discovery checked commit availability and repository documentation. This sample covers three American collecting institutions and does not support a population-wide claim about museums.

For each object table take the last data-file commit on the publisher's default branch as of midnight UTC on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, and 1 October 2026. Use the GitHub commits API with the file path and until parameter. Record exact SHAs, commit dates, Git blob hashes, SHA-256 content digests, headers, number of records, and uniqueness of the publisher's object key. For Git LFS downloads verify the pointer's SHA-256 and size. Release discovery supplies no compression scores. Keep downloaded tables in the ignored raw data directory. Do not discard repeated releases or require a minimum number of edits. If the same SHA repeats, retain the repeated release in the inventory. All consecutive pairs form the paired study with no best-interval selection.

The receiver knows the source table, the schema and fixed decoder. The encoder must transmit every data-dependent choice. Preserve the full publisher table under the existing canonical representation with the identity field first and remaining columns in their published order. Fields are UTF-8 strings after parsing CSV. Audit duplicate keys and header changes. Any incompatible layout, including a schema change unsupported by a codec, must be reported with its interval. A schema or decoder failure prevents an all-interval superiority claim. A future schema-handling extension must charge any schema description to every applicable method and be specified before measurement.

Before scoring, freeze the candidate, decoder, ablations, command lines and comparator list including xdelta3, bsdiff, HDiffPatch, own-cell and within-row patching. Confirm the Tate development gate first. A byte-for-byte reconstruction is mandatory for every wire. Evaluate the total wire bytes for the frozen candidate and every comparator on each interval. The criterion is a reduction of at least 5% against each comparator in every reserved interval, including the matched simpler methods. Preserve all individual bytes and failures. The pre-specified provider-level effect is one minus total candidate bytes divided by total comparator bytes across that provider's three intervals. Report both each provider's estimate and their equal-weight mean. A single publisher is the independent cluster because successive intervals share a catalogue and release process. Three providers are insufficient to show a one-sided sign-test p below .05 even for three successes (best p=.125). Passing the descriptive interval screen provides external evidence but requires additional independent institutions for a publication-level uncertainty claim. Do not use files, record examples or outcomes from these releases to tune a codec. Development remains confined to Tate.

This local protocol preceded data-body acquisition and any codec run on this panel. Its checksum is an integrity check without independent timestamping.
